prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. Earlier searches scored 0 on dev and on training success in 84 of 84 trials. That means the agent never finishes an exact build, so the bottleneck is optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. Several things in the data point to DONE as a trap. DONE is sampled mostly while cells are still missing, where it earns 0 against positive rewards for placing bricks, so its logit is pushed down everywhere. When the build is finally complete, DONE is almost never chosen. The fix is to make "a missing cell still exists" easy to read: a learned 1x1 layer on the observation, then a max over the grid, feeding the DONE head. Other ideas not yet tried are initialisation hygiene (orthogonal init, near-uniform starting policy), GroupNorm, a raw-observation skip into the placement head, factorised logits and recipe extremes. The six candidates below differ in trunk (residual, column MLP, deep narrow, U-Net, head-heavy) and recipe (1 to 4 epochs), and each stacks several fixes.

### Round 2
All six round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That matches the 84 earlier trials and the starting architecture. These trials stacked four kinds of change: initialisation hygiene, GroupNorm, a raw-obs skip and factorised logits. The recipes ranged from 1 to 3 epochs, 108k to 405k steps, lr up to 3e-3 and gamma up to 0.995. None of this was enough. Because training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build, so the bottleneck is per-step precision, not generalisation. Every footprint head so far pooled features independently per channel. None let each covered cell be judged against a landing layer that depends on the whole footprint. That check needs two stages: footprint → anchor → each covered cell → logical AND. This round tests that relational head on several trunks and recipes. It also tests multiplicative (GLU) features for AND-like logic, shared per-layer voxel features with a learned soft choice of landing layer, and a myopic, bandit-like recipe. Every candidate stacks several changes.

### Round 3
All 12 trials in this search scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That makes 96 trials across searches with no signal, including dense, attention and relational heads, voxel and landing-softmax heads, GroupNorm, init hygiene and recipe extremes. Because training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build even with sampled actions. The problem is optimisation or perception, not generalisation. The world is altered in some unstated way. Plausible changes include a mismatch between the action layout and the observation layout (flip, rotation or transpose), a different anchor or footprint convention, or a need for long-range spatial reasoning. So this round tests new families aimed at those hypotheses. They are dihedral multi-branch heads, offset-tolerant grouped 5x5 heads over every footprint's pooling, cheap global token mixing (Mixer), a weight-shared build-vs-target encoder, and a weight-tied recurrent trunk. The last candidate stacks most of these with a learnable output remap and per-action biases. Each candidate keeps r at or below about 1.45.

### Round 4
After 18 trials in this search and 84 earlier ones, every trial has scored 0, on dev and on training success. None of the ideas tested so far has worked: new heads (relational, landing-softmax, dihedral, offset-tolerant, remap), new trunks (GN-residual, U-Net, token-mixing, Siamese, weight-tied, GLU), initialisation fixes, and recipe extremes. With training success at 0 everywhere, the agent never finishes an exact build. That points to a systematic problem in this world, not to a small loss of efficiency. This is the last round. To maximise the chance of any nonzero signal, all six candidates share one base: a GN-residual trunk, a raw skip, a footprint head aligned to each type's own footprint, and an offset-tolerant head that pools under every footprint shape. Each candidate then tests an axis not yet tried: about 3x capacity; soft-capped logits with maximum entropy; very large batches; a learned remap that can mix logits across types; a stack of everything; and many epochs with small clipping.

## Trial it ended with
name: Soft-capped logits, max entropy
hypothesis: If the policy collapses early, for example to an early DONE or to one wrong placement habit, exploration never finds an exact build. Soft-capping the logits (8*tanh(l/8)) bounds how deterministic the policy can become. Entropy is set to 0.05, the bound and above anything tried, and gamma to 0.99. The base is the dual-head GN net. Refuted if training and dev success stay 0.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: Round 3 names the right kind of change but not its details.
